hud_fmr.name: HUD Fair Market Rents, FY2026, one bedroom, county and metro areas
hud_fmr.note: HUD's ArcGIS feature service of the FMR data (layer modified 2026-04-20; 2622 areas). A county takes the rent of its HUD metro area (Census CBSA delineation, July 2023) or its own non-metro area; for a county in a metro area that HUD splits under older codes, the mean of that metro area's HUD areas. huduser.gov answers a scripted client with a bot challenge, so its xlsx files were not used.

acs_b25088.name: Census ACS 2020-2024 5-year, table B25088: median selected monthly owner costs, by mortgage status
acs_b25088.note: Table-based summary file (the Census API asks for a key). Owner costs include mortgage, taxes, insurance, utilities and fees. The table has no age split, so the figure is for all owners.

acs_b01003.name: Census ACS 2020-2024 5-year, table B01003: total population (the weights for place medians)

cbsa.name: Census CBSA delineation, July 2023 (county to metro area)

usda_low_cost.name: USDA Food Plans: Cost of Food at Home, Low-Cost Plan, October 2026, individuals in 4-person households
usda_low_cost.note: Machine-readable file: https://www.fns.usda.gov/sites/default/files/resource-files/usda-lowcostplan-sept2007-oct2026.xlsx. Household-size adjustment as the report states it: one person +20%, two persons +10%.

fhwa_nhts.name: FHWA 2017 National Household Travel Survey, Summary of Travel Trends, Table 23b: average annual miles per licensed driver, by age and sex (self-estimate)
fhwa_nhts.note: Drivers 65 and older. The 2022 summary has no such table. Miles are the driver's own estimate.

irs_mileage.name: IRS standard mileage rate, 2026
irs_mileage.note: Business rates in cents: 76.0, 72.5 (two half-year rates in 2026); the mean is used. The rate covers fuel, repairs, insurance, depreciation and tax on driving.

health.name: Medicare Part B and Part D premiums and out-of-pocket health spending
health.note: Not copied here. engine/basics_benchmark.py reads data/health_costs.json (CMS), so the benchmark and the plan share one health figure.

cms_nhe_age_2020.name: CMS Office of the Actuary, National Health Expenditure Accounts by age and sex, Table 7-1: Out-of-Pocket Per-capita Spending by Sex and Age Group (workbook 'Age20 tables 3-27-24.xlsx')
cms_nhe_age_2020.published: 2024-03-27 (data through calendar year 2020, the latest year published)
cms_nhe_age_2020.note: Read from the downloaded workbook. Per-capita out-of-pocket PERSONAL HEALTH CARE spending (deductibles, coinsurance, copays and uncovered services, including nursing-home out-of-pocket; premiums are NOT out-of-pocket in NHE). 2020 is a pandemic year with depressed use: 2018 values are kept beside 2020 (19-44 $688, 45-64 $1,418, 65-84 $2,513, 85+ $6,404) and are within 5% for 45+. Nominal dollars, restated to today with the CPI-U ratio, which understates medical price growth if medical prices rose faster than the CPI.

cms_medicare_2027.name: CMS fact sheet: 2027 Medicare Parts A & B Premiums and Deductibles
cms_medicare_2027.note: Standard Part B premium $209.40, Part B deductible $292, Part A deductible $1,776, and the 2027 IRMAA tables for Part B and Part D (MAGI from two years earlier, so 2025 income). Matches the Federal Register notice FR Doc. 2026-23601 (published 2026-11-19, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/19/2026-23601/medicare-program-medicare-part-b-monthly-actuarial-rates-premium-rates-and-annual-deductible): $209.40, $292, actuarial rates $418.70 aged and $452.40 disabled.

kff_part_d_2026.name: KFF, Medicare Part D Enrollment, Premiums, and Cost Sharing in 2026
kff_part_d_2026.note: Average monthly stand-alone PDP premium $36 (MA-PD $8); national base beneficiary premium $38.99; 2026 out-of-pocket drug cap $2,100. Read from a search summary of the KFF pages, not the pages themselves; the $2,400 cap for 2027 is from one secondary source (low confidence).
